The test image shows a corn ear with extensive white mycelium growing over and between kernels, with the cob tissue heavily damaged and grayish-brown. This is characteristic of Diplodia ear rot: white mold covering kernels, starting from the base/middle of the ear, with deteriorated cob tissue. The some greenish patches visible are likely secondary colonization. This distinguishes it from Gibberella (pink-red mold at tip), Fusarium (scattered cottony mold on individual kernels), Trichoderma (dark green mold), and Aspergillus (olive-green powdery mold).
